evidence.note: Opening work is test-harness exploration and environment probing, not milestone/feature-sequencing. No ordered progression of language features is laid out anywhere.
Compiler is written via two large apply_patch edits in bulk rather than staged by feature milestone (no return-int→expressions→variables progression visible).
Progress is checked by running the full 780-test run_tests.sh, not against per-feature test subsets that would certify individual milestones.
Post-build work is reactive, failure-by-failure debugging (page-boundary tests, gcc-torture cases) with no completion criteria tied to feature dependencies.

reasoning: The observed trajectory shows bulk compiler construction followed by full-suite runs and test-by-test debugging, with no explicit dependency-ordered milestone plan, no named per-feature done-signals, and no staged test subsets — placing it near anchor 0 (whole-language/feature-to-feature). It rises slightly above pure 0 because the agent front-loaded test-harness understanding and repeatedly re-ran the suite to gauge progress, but this is full-suite checking rather than the staged, per-milestone verification described at anchor 3+. Hence a 2.
